title: Saddle
text: “So, what do you think about that whole thing with Itsuki?”

It seems Itsuki took part in the revolution, but the revolutionary forces, once they seized power, apparently broke their campaign promises. I suppose that’s why Itsuki left it all to the revolutionary forces and walked away. And that’s how we ended up in the current situation, right?
“It seems like there are a lot of shortcomings. Well, I’m not one to talk, though.”
“I don’t really get why Motoyasu-kun is walking around with his chest puffed out.”
“Boo…”
The Lazy Pig muttered something under his breath.
“Elena… you shouldn’t say things that completely ruin the mood.”
“What did he say, exactly?”
“‘Despite the high taxes, they jumped at short-term gains. It’s their own fault…’ is what he said.”
“That’s ridiculous—but he’s absolutely right.”
For a Lazy Pig, he sure has a way with words. As I clapped my hands and laughed, my Father spoke up.
“Motoyasu-kun!”
My Father scolded me. I’m extremely dissatisfied, but I don’t think I’m wrong.

In other words, the reason for the heavy taxes wasn’t that the king was living in luxury, but simply that he was demanding the minimum expenditure necessary to maintain the country. Knowing Itsuki as I do, it’s easy to imagine that he joined the revolution without even checking the facts properly.

“If Itsuki was involved in the revolution, that would’ve spurred the revolutionary army on even more, so it was practically bound to succeed… is that about right? But… look at the result. It’s obvious at a glance that Itsuki didn’t do his research. Just like me, he probably only listened to the side that seemed to be the underdog. There was an episode like that in the Book of the Four Holy Weapons, too.”
“Boo.”

“Ah, yeah… Probably black-market rice… smuggled in, I guess. Because of the revolution, they have neither money nor goods, so from a merchant’s perspective, it might be best to abandon them. But still… even if we send them a wagon loaded with food, it’ll probably be tough for them to cross the border.”
My father let out a deep sigh and nodded as if making a decision. The Lazy Pig said something to my father with a look of exasperation.
“I know, it’s a long shot. I’ll just think of it as an investment in the future and let it go.”
“Oink…”
“Yeah, I doubt we’ll get anything in return.”
My father went to hand the customer some bio-plant seeds for sale.
“What’s this?”

“These are magic seeds that’ll make the vegetables you just ate bear fruit right away. Just be careful, though. If you don’t all put your hearts into growing them properly, they’ll wither right away. These should be easy to carry, right?”
“Eh… uh…”
Father held up a finger as if to signal “secret.”
“If you ever become wealthy thanks to these seeds, please help someone else just as much as you were helped back then.”
“Y-yes!”

The illegal immigrant kept expressing his gratitude for Father’s sincerity. After finishing distributing the food, Father returned to the carriage. We followed him and climbed into the carriage as well.
“This should be about right.”
“Boo.”
“All right, all right. I know that’s not how a businessman should act.”
“You’re so cool, bro.”
“Keel, don’t get your eyes all sparkling. It’s not really a good thing… I actually want you to buy some to take home.”
My Father looks a bit tired.
“Am I being too soft…? Hmm…”
“Naofumi—that’s exactly what makes you great.”
“That’s right! No matter what, he’s the one who keeps everyone safe—that’s my Father for you.”
“That’s a relief to hear. Well then… I’ve sold off a fair amount of my stock, so what should I do next?”
“There’s still some time before the next wave.”

All things considered, the crowd has thinned out quite a bit by the time the next wave hits. Even so, we still have time. After all, the kidnapping of my Finacée happened right after we dealt with the previous wave. If we can buy enough time until then, it’ll be the end for the Trash, the Crimson Swine, and the Three Heroes Church. The time to finally mete out justice to those bastards is drawing near.
“For now, let’s keep doing what we’ve been doing—stock up at Elena’s place and continue peddling.”
“I think that’s for the best. Father, has your wallet gotten a bit fuller?”
“Well, sort of…”

Father pointed to the money bags inside the carriage. Since we’ve earned quite a bit from our trading so far, there’s a substantial amount there. By the way, I hear the Lazy Pig has a complete grasp of the current total.

He’s only clever when it comes to money and lazing around, isn’t he? If he were an enemy, I’d have killed him with a single blow by now. But since he’s actually being useful to Father, let’s let him off the hook this time as a special exception.
“I think there’s enough to buy new weapons and armor for Keel and the others. We’ll have to buy gear for Wyndia-chan and Gaelion-chan, too.”
“Gau?”
“What do you want, Gaelion-chan?”
“Gau!”
It seems the assistant is translating the monster’s words. Hmph, a dragon’s weapons are probably nothing more than claws. After all, dragons can only breathe fire and attack with their claws.

In that regard, Filolial-sama possesses a variety of attack methods. Sakura-chan uses dual swords, Yuki-chan and Kou use claws, and Luna-chan hasn’t decided yet. Also, Ku breathes fire, Marine uses Magic and her wings, and Midori became an angel and used an axe. You can see at a glance just how much more impressive they are compared to dragons.
“Motoyasu-kun, I know what you’re thinking, but I’m sure there’s not much difference between the two.”
“That’s not true. They’ll probably just say ‘claws’ or ‘fangs’ anyway.”
“Nope, she wants a saddle.”
“A saddle…? Why?”
“Gau!”
“So the Shield Hero and I can ride safely.”
“Boo!”
Sakura-chan is objecting. I’ll back Sakura-chan up, too.
“Sakura wants a saddle, too!”
“Don’t compete with her. Sakura-chan is good at carrying people, so just the reins should be enough, right?”
“But I want one! I won’t lose to Gaelion!”
“I want one, too.”
“What are you going to do with a saddle, Motoyasu-kun?!”
“I’ll get down on all fours and carry my Father.”
“Motoyasu-kun, why don’t you keep it down a bit?”
“Gau gau!”
Sakura-chan and the monster started glaring at each other, sparks flying. I’ll join in, too. I’ll set my sights on the Assistant. She quickly looked away from me. I won.
“Motoyasu-kun doesn’t like to compete.”
“Well then, shall I take the rope from my Father and wrap it around my body? I’ll be tied up in a tortoise-shell bondage and rolled into the carriage.”
“Someone! Please pour water on Motoyasu-kun. He’s been saying strange things for a while now.”
Oh? Did I say something strange? I’m getting annoyed that Keel poured water on me.
“It’s a matter of loyalty to my Father. By inflicting pain on myself, I’m atoning for my sins toward him.”
“Oh, yeah, yeah—save that for my future self. Don’t do it now.”

Oh, my. My Father just mentioned a future that’s now completely impossible. What a painful thing to say! I can no longer apologize to my future Father. So, to earn forgiveness from my present Father, I’m punishing myself.
“Getting back to the saddle… Does Gaelion really need one? She only lets me and Wyndia ride her.”
“Gau?”
“I think it’s better to have one if you’re going to ride a dragon.”
“Hmm, well, let’s buy one next time, then. If we pick up some claws or fangs while we’re at it, we’ll be prepared for anything. What kind of weapon do you want, Wyndia?”
“Gau!”
“Me? Hmm… Since I’m in charge of Magic, maybe a staff?”

Come to think of it, my Assistant was good at Magic. By the way, when I say “Magic,” I mean the Way of the Dragon Vein. In that case, a staff would be the safest choice for my Assistant’s weapon. But did my Assistant even carry a staff in the first world?
I can’t quite remember. She was always riding a Caterpilland or a Gaelion. Could it be… her bare hands?
“That’s true. Well then, let’s ask the old man at the weapon shop to make us a staff. Or maybe I should ask at the magic shop instead?”
“I don’t really know.”
“Boo…”
“Oh, so we’ll ask at the magic shop? That lady at the magic shop seems like a nice person, so let’s give it a try.”
“Yeah.”

That’s settled, then. With this, my Assistant should be at least somewhat useful in battle. It’s frustrating, but the dragon is Filolial-sama’s rival. And since it’s a rival, it’s only natural that it has its own abilities.
“Big bro! What about me?”
“What about Sakura?”
“After the second wave, something’s bound to happen. And it’ll be an incident with the Three Heroes Church involved behind the scenes.”
“In that case… maybe there’s no need to hide it anymore?”
“So, is it okay to bring weapons from over there?”

Once we get past the second wave, there’ll be no need to hide our weapons and armor anymore. By the way, the gear we’re using in Siltvelt is stored at the inn we’ve been renting long-term over there. We’ve got more money than we know what to do with over there, and since it’s a locked inn, there’s no worry about it getting stolen.
“Sakura wants weapons from over there, too.”

“Yeah, you’re right. So, how about we go pick up those weapons the day before the wave hits? I’d actually like Dad to make us some weapons, though. While we’re out on patrol, let’s also swing by the town below Melromarc Castle.”

Our plan was starting to take shape. With those thoughts in mind, we returned to the Lazy Pig’s territory. Little did we know at the time that hearing a certain story there would cause us to abruptly change our course.
